turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again? I was on the wrong tab.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes. Knee.
[SEG0004] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, I am Meena, I stay with him and help in the house. The right knee is the problem. It catches him on the stairs.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Mr. Iyer, in your own words, what is paining?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): Pain.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Where? One second, the cursor has jumped.
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Knee. Right.
[SEG0009] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Going down the stairs is the worst. And he wakes at night with it, doctor.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Since when has this been?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Diwali. Or after.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which year? Can you date it?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): Cannot. Last winter. Or the one before.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Diwali, or last winter, or the one before. Alright, we will leave the date. Does the knee swell?
[SEG0015] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It swells, doctor. By evening it is puffy.
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): You are saying no swelling, she says puffy. Which is it?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0019] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I have seen it puffy myself. He will not admit it.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any giving way, or locking?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fever? Knee feeling hot?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the stomach? Any acidity, vomiting, with the pain tablets?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come again? No what? This fan and the system both are noisy.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Stomach.
[SEG0028] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He does get heartburn, though. After those chemist tablets.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mr. Iyer, is there heartburn or not? Please say it once more.
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Heartburn. Sometimes.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): So heartburn, sometimes. What medicine are you actually using?
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): Gel.
[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Diclofenac gel, one percent. He rubs it on the knee morning and night.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the tablets from the chemist?
[SEG0035] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Diclofenac tablets, by mouth. Fifty milligram, one at night, most days. I give it after milk.
[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): Sometimes.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): The strength, please repeat. I typed in the wrong box.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Fifty milligram.
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): Twenty.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fifty from her, twenty from you. I will not record a dose till that is clear. Any other tablets?
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): Pressure.
[SEG0042] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Amlodipine, five milligram, by mouth, one in the morning. For the blood pressure. Five-ish years now.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Five milligram amlodipine, once each morning, for about five years. Any allergy to a drug, or a food?
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nothing noted there. On the screen the blood pressure is one-forty over eighty-eight, the pulse is seventy-six, and the weight is eighty-four point five kilos.
[SEG0046] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He has put on, doctor. It is the sweets.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Eighty-four point five is sitting high for this knee. We should talk about that weight.
[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): Hmm.

[SEG0049] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Before I forget, his grandson hit a century in the school match on Sunday. We were stuck near Silk Board for an hour, and then the rain started. He spoke only of that cover drive the whole way.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): A century at school level, that is lovely. Silk Board in the rain is a proper punishment. I missed the last over myself, the wifi at home just died.
[SEG0051] person_3 (CAREGIVER): We made masala chai and pakoras after. Now the boy wants an English willow bat. Very costly, that one.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Those bats are a fortune, truly. Right, back to the knee. It is not warm, there is crepitus when you bend, and I do not feel an effusion.
[SEG0053] person_1 (PATIENT): Ow.
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry. Pain on the stairs and at night, with that crepitus, this is most likely osteoarthritis. I am not putting a final stamp on it today.
[SEG0055] person_1 (PATIENT): Okay.
[SEG0056] person_2 (DOCTOR): We could try physiotherapy, or a steroid injection into the knee. I am not deciding which one today. Either one only if the gel is not enough.
[SEG0057] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Which is better, doctor?
[SEG0058] person_2 (DOCTOR): I cannot say yet. Please stop the diclofenac tablets. Continue the gel, morning and night. Kindly cut the sweets, the weight will not help this knee.
[SEG0059] person_1 (PATIENT): Gel only.
[SEG0060] person_2 (DOCTOR): Gel only, yes. Come back in six weeks. We will choose the physio or the injection at that visit.
[SEG0061] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Six weeks. I will bring him. Thank you, doctor.
[SEG0062] person_1 (PATIENT): Thanks.
[SEG0063] person_2 (DOCTOR): Take care. Meena, if the strip of tablets is still at home, bring it next time so we can see the strength.
